text:
maria: Ran a focused perf run this morning — trying a "surgical" partial-quant strategy: 4-bit on attention matrices, INT8 on FFN, and explicit excludes for embeddings + lm_head. Results look off: ~20% lower throughput vs the INT8 baseline and higher tail latency on cached requests. :thinking:

devon: Can you paste the exact config you used? curious if kernel selection is thrashing between quant kernels and fp16 fallbacks.

maria: Sure, here's the snippet I used:
```
partial_quant:
  exclude_layers: ["embed_tokens", "lm_head"]
  quant_map:
    attention: int4
    ffn: int8
  sensitive_threshold: 0.025
  enable_layer_calibration: true
```

kasia: Two immediate suspects: 1) calibration pass overhead (if done per-batch) and 2) kernel selection heuristics that flip when sequence length or KV cache size varies. Did perfbot attach kernel selection traces? :eyes:

perfbot: Attached profile: kernel-switch spikes at ~seq_len=64 boundaries; ~30% of requests triggered fallback to fp16 kernels for blocks 3..5. KV cache hit latencies show a bimodal distribution. Link: https://perf.internal/runs/1779/summary

lee: The bimodal KV latency usually means batching is mixing cold prefixes with hot ones. When the batch includes a long prefix, the KV tensors get larger and we pick a different kernel (different memory pattern) which then takes longer for other items in the same batch.

maria: Hmm I did run with dynamic batching turned on (max_batch=32, max_latency_ms=12). Maybe the batcher merged heterogeneous prefixes. Any quick mitigations?

devon: Try prefix-aware batching (split by prefix_hash mod N) to avoid mixing very different kv sizes. Also add a kernel-selection hysteresis: prefer staying on chosen kernel for X steps unless mem pressure forces switch. That reduces oscillation.

kasia: Also check calibration mode — if enable_layer_calibration=true triggers per-request stats, that'll slow things down. Use an offline/staged calibration: sample a corpus, compute quant parameters, then lock them. Calibration costs often overlooked.

maria: Good call. I think the config accidentally did live calibration. I'll rerun with offline calibration and prefix-aware batching. Any thoughts on sensitive-layer detection? I don't want to manually whitelist thousands of layers.

lee: We can compute a cheap sensitivity metric: run a single microbatch with small FP32 perturbations per layer and measure output delta (L2 on logits) / perf delta. Flag layers with delta_loss > threshold. We did this in the old ablation tool. Might be able to run it in ~5–10 mins for 8k params model.

devon: If that micro-sensitivity pass is still expensive, do a two-pass heuristic: 1) coarse pass on grouped layers (embed, early-attn, mid-attn, late-attn, ffn groups), 2) refine only groups that fail threshold. Cuts work by ~5x.

maria: Nice. I'll try grouped-sensitivity + offline calib + prefix-aware batching. One more question: kernel selection policy — is there a flag to bias toward quant kernels even if they cost a bit more memory but are faster on our HW? Right now selection seems purely latency-estimate driven and sometimes picks fp16 because memory estimate is lower.

devon: We recently added a config knob in runtime: `kernel_selection_policy = "latency_weighted|memory_weighted|stability_weighted"`. Stability_weighted prefers kernels that have historically lower variance. Try `stability_weighted` then reduce oscillation.

maria: Great, I'll run three variants: (A) offline calib + grouped sensitivity + prefix-batching + stability_weighted, (B) same but force fp16 on top-5 sensitive layers, (C) baseline partial quant with offline calib only. Will post numbers.

ops-bot: Scheduled a canary job for maria to /canary/quant-surgical-1779 with 5% traffic at 18:00 UTC.

perfbot: Ping when you have run ids and I'll auto-aggregate kernel traces and KV latency histograms.

maria: Thanks all — kicking off A/B/C now. Will update with the run links and a short table. :thumbsup:
